cohort: The study included 43 singleton pregnant patients who experienced spontaneous preterm birth (23 conceived after IVF/ICSI, 20 naturally conceived) and 10 healthy control patients who had term births.
finding: Amniotic fluid proinflammatory cytokine levels (NF-kB, TNF-a, IL-1b, IL-6) were similar between sPTB patients regardless of conception method (IVF/ICSI vs. natural) and were also similar to healthy controls with term delivery, suggesting a common underlying mechanism for sPTB.
mod_finding: There was no difference in amniotic fluid proinflammatory cytokine levels between patients who delivered vaginally or by cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Amniotic fluid samples were collected at the time of spontaneous preterm labor/delivery or term delivery, either following spontaneous/artificial rupture of membranes or just before cesarean section.
birth_weight: Fetal birth weight was similar in the IVF/ICSI and natural conception groups, but specific ranges for inclusion are not mentioned.
gest_age: Patients with spontaneous preterm birth were included if delivery occurred before 37 weeks, and gestational age at delivery was similar between the IVF/ICSI and natural conception groups.
